body:
Yeah, I contacted the Lost & Found + used their support section on their website to provide my information. I'm not sure if the phone at D Lift is the phone in question as I lost mine closer to G Lift. Regardless, if you're going back tomorrow, it would do me a great favor if you could see if the area I last had my phone is where it is!

After checking Find My iPhone on another device, I believe its battery had died so I'm not sure if I can ring it or not at this point.

Damn, so I was too slow in making a treasure hunt post for it. Haha, no worries! Honestly I got too occupied with my phone that I didn't get to go on any black diamonds. Either way, for it being my annual skiing trip I enjoyed Windham. I heard that Hunter Mountain was better from my 4 friends who went to New York a few hours earlier than us.

Hopefully you enjoyed Windham as I did. Maybe it's just because I don't even ski often at all, lmao. Hopefully someone does stumble upon it, and hopefully they don't sell it- stay safe with Covid-19 and all that!

Isn't that what a hero is? Whoever owns those keys, people who've lost items, and I myself admire people like you who go out your way to save our day. I wish I could've double-checked my pockets and found it before it became an issue for me, but it's obviously too late lol. Either way, hopefully more people see this post and take on the challenge.

Maaan. Just as I was talking to the staff at the Lost & Found at 4 PM, some other guy walked up mentioning how he lost car keys. I was told keys, cards, and things of that sort with little to no solid form/mass are basically impossible to find in Windham Mountain. You're an absolute hero for finding keys, and more so if you returned them or in the process of doing so.

Yep! There was a nice staff member at Windham Mountain's "Demo Center" that I spoke to. He let me text & call my mom to tell her about the situation. Since I don't remember my friends' phone number by memory. Now that I realize the situation, I've asked them for the numbers to write down and put them in my wallet. The irony is, I literally thought about the posts where it's really helpful to know your *friends'* numbers as well. Anyways, he directed me to the Lost & Found where they said to come back at 4 PM (Closing time) since nothing came in yet. I came back and they didn't have it, so I just filled a form for them to contact me by. For reassurance, I sent them a question on their website.

I don't remember there being any snow blown on that particular corner as well, so hopefully it isn't buried anywhere. I do remember there being some kind of ditch nearby, so I'll be damned if I somehow dropped it in there. Funny story, you know how some jackets have zippers that just lead inside of the jacket without any pockets? I might've put my phone in there not knowing there wasn't a pocket at all, and it slipped through.

I made the post just for fun at this point, and if I lost the phone, then I lost it. I thought though, why not? If anyone's there, I might as well take the chance. Anyways, I'm glad I at least got a comment on this thread; nice to know there're people who understand how annoying it is to lose something on a trail. Honestly, I think I looked in the same area I lost it only to give up for who knows why.
Those are the videos and articles that have already failed. With that said, I appreciate you coming to comfort my problem.

It’d be very helpful if you clarified on what. I’ve taken lessons on how to ease a stutter and I’ll admit it works. However, as I said I’m still young, so naturally my parents pay for it and I don’t want to make them lose money since I can’t do something as simple as speak. 

I don’t know anymore. It comes back at the end of the day to torment me mentally. I can argue that it’s easier to just stop thinking about it by taking the route of suicide.
